# JIRA Import Implementation Checklist
## Pre-Import Preparation
### Database Setup - [ ] Verify all reporter/assignee users exist in database - [ ] Check that first_name and last_name fields are properly populated - [ ] For dot-separated names (e.g., archana.verma), ensure database has matching first_name and last_name - [ ] Review users with multi-part names (3+ parts) - verify first 2 parts match database - [ ] Create any missing users before import
### Configuration - [ ] Set `create_missing_users: true` or `false` in config/jira_import.yml - [ ] Add manual user mappings if needed for known edge cases - [ ] Verify DEFAULT_USER_UUID is set to a valid user - [ ] Test Jira API credentials (JIRA_API_TOKEN)
### Testing - [ ] Run: `rails runner scripts/test_user_matching.rb` - [ ] Review output - all parsing tests should pass - [ ] Verify that test users are found in database
## Import Phase
### Dry-Run - [ ] Run: `rails runner scripts/import_jira_with_modules.rb --project PROJECTKEY --dry-run` - [ ] Review the user match statistics report - [ ] Check for fallback to default user - note which issues are affected - [ ] Verify parsing strategies used (dot-separated, multi-part, etc.) - [ ] If needed, create missing users and re-run dry-run
### Actual Import - [ ] Run: `rails runner scripts/import_jira_with_modules.rb --project PROJECTKEY` - [ ] Monitor for errors (check console output) - [ ] Note the final user match statistics - [ ] Identify any issues with fallback to default user
## Post-Import Verification
### Automated Verification - [ ] Run: `rails runner scripts/verify_and_fix_user_assignments.rb` - [ ] Review the verification report - [ ] Check how many issues were auto-fixed - [ ] Note any issues that couldn't be fixed
### Manual Review - [ ] Query database for issues with default user assignment - [ ] Sample check: pick 5 random issues and verify reporter/assignee match Jira - [ ] Check attachment download status (from import report) - [ ] Verify all labels were attached correctly
### Report Analysis - [ ] Look for patterns in unmatched names - [ ] Identify common name formats not handled well - [ ] Check for case sensitivity issues - [ ] Review any parsing strategy failures
## Troubleshooting (if needed)
### Unmatched Names - [ ] Check exact spelling in both Jira and database - [ ] For dot-separated: verify format is "first.last" - [ ] For multi-part: verify first 2 parts match database - [ ] Check for special characters or extra spaces - [ ] Create missing users and re-run verification
### Fallback to Default - [ ] Review which issues were affected - [ ] Manually assign correct users if needed - [ ] Or create missing users and run verification again
### Parsing Issues - [ ] Check if names match expected formats - [ ] Add custom parsing logic if needed (modify parse_jira_name function) - [ ] Test changes with test_user_matching.rb - [ ] Re-run import if changes were needed
## Final Cleanup
### Data Validation - [ ] Verify total number of imported issues matches Jira count - [ ] Check that no issues have nil reporter (except if Jira had none) - [ ] Verify attachments are accessible (spot check a few) - [ ] Confirm all comments were imported
### Documentation - [ ] Document any custom name parsing added - [ ] Note any manual fixes applied - [ ] Record any issues with the import - [ ] Update user mapping config for future imports
### Archive Results - [ ] Save import reports to archive - [ ] Document final statistics - [ ] Create backup of changes - [ ] Prepare rollback plan (if needed)
## Sign-Off
- [ ] Import completed successfully - [ ] User assignments verified - [ ] All issues accessible - [ ] Attachments working - [ ] Team notified of completion - [ ] System ready for production use
---
## Checklist for Each Project Import
When importing multiple projects, repeat this checklist for each:
### Project: _________________
#### Pre-Import - [ ] Database users exist - [ ] Configuration updated - [ ] Test parsing (if first time)
#### Import - [ ] Dry-run passed - [ ] Actual import ran - [ ] Review final report
#### Post-Import - [ ] Verification script run - [ ] Issues reviewed - [ ] Manual fixes applied (if any)
#### Sign-Off - [ ] Ready for production - [ ] Team notified
---
## Common Issues Quick Reference
| Issue | Cause | Solution | |-------|-------|----------| | Name falls back to default | User doesn't exist | Create user in database | | Dot-separated not matching | Wrong database format | Ensure first_name and last_name are separate | | Multi-part name fails | Using wrong parts | Verify first 2 parts match database | | Case sensitivity | Case mismatch | Check database consistency | | Email not matching | Extra spaces or domain issue | Verify exact email match |
## Useful Commands
```bash # Test name parsing rails runner scripts/test_user_matching.rb
# Dry-run import rails runner scripts/import_jira_with_modules.rb --project KCBL --dry-run --verbose
# Actual import rails runner scripts/import_jira_with_modules.rb --project KCBL
# Verify and fix assignments rails runner scripts/verify_and_fix_user_assignments.rb
# Check for issues with default user rails c > Defect.joins(:users).where(users: { id: 'default-user-id' }).count
# Find issues with nil assignee rails c > Defect.where('NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM defect_users WHERE defect_id = defects.id)').count ```
## Notes
- All matching is **case-insensitive** - Email matching takes priority over name matching - Multi-part names use **first 2 parts only** - Dot-separated format: **"first.last"** - Default user assignment is **tracked and reported** - Verification script can **auto-fix** most mismatches
---
**Status**: Ready for implementation
**Last Updated**: November 27, 2025
**Next Review**: After first project import

# Multi-Part Name Matching Examples
## Scenario 1: Two-Part Name (Works as Before) ``` JIRA Name: "John Smith" Parsed As: first_name="John", last_name="Smith" Combinations: None (uses original logic)
Database Search Order: 1. first_name="john" AND last_name="smith" [EXACT MATCH] 2. first_name="john" AND last_name LIKE "smith%" [PARTIAL] 3. last_name="smith" AND first_name LIKE "john%" [PARTIAL]
Result: ✅ Matched (or ❌ Fallback) ```
---
## Scenario 2: Three-Part Name (NEW - Multiple Strategies) ``` JIRA Name: "Eva Karimi Njagi" Parsed As: first_name="Eva", last_name="Karimi" Combinations: [["Eva", "Karimi"], ["Eva", "Njagi"], ["Karimi", "Njagi"]]
Strategy 1 - Try Eva + Karimi: ├─ first_name="eva" AND last_name="karimi" [EXACT MATCH] ├─ first_name="eva" AND last_name LIKE "kar%" [PARTIAL] └─ last_name="karimi" AND first_name LIKE "eva%" [PARTIAL]
If no match, Strategy 2 - Try Eva + Njagi: ├─ first_name="eva" AND last_name="njagi" [EXACT MATCH] ├─ first_name="eva" AND last_name LIKE "nja%" [PARTIAL] └─ last_name="njagi" AND first_name LIKE "eva%" [PARTIAL]
If no match, Strategy 3 - Try Karimi + Njagi: ├─ first_name="karimi" AND last_name="njagi" [EXACT MATCH] ├─ first_name="karimi" AND last_name LIKE "nja%" [PARTIAL] └─ last_name="njagi" AND first_name LIKE "kar%" [PARTIAL]
Result: ✅ Matched on Strategy X (or ❌ Fallback) ```
---
## Scenario 3: Four-Part Name (NEW - Multiple Strategies) ``` JIRA Name: "John David Smith Jones" Parsed As: first_name="John", last_name="David" Combinations: [["John", "David"], ["John", "Smith"], ["David", "Jones"], ["John", "Jones"]]
Strategy 1 - Try John + David Strategy 2 - Try John + Smith Strategy 3 - Try David + Jones Strategy 4 - Try John + Jones
Result: ✅ Matched on Strategy X (or ❌ Fallback) ```
---
## Real-World Example: Stephen Mungai
### Before This Fix ``` JIRA Name: "Stephen Mungai" Problem: Only tried "Stephen" + "Mungai" If no database entry for "Stephen Mungai" → FALLBACK TO DEFAULT USER (49 times!)
Statistics: - Lookups: 49 - Matches: 0 - Fallbacks: 49 (100%) ```
### After This Fix ``` JIRA Name: "Stephen Mungai" Parsing: Parts = ["Stephen", "Mungai"] Result: 2 parts → Use original strategy (same as before)
However, if "Stephen Mungai" doesn't exist but the database has: - "Stephen" as first_name and "Mungai" as last_name (partial match) → ✅ MATCHED! - "Stephen" as last_name and "Mungai" as first_name (reversed) → ✅ MATCHED!
Expected Improvement: - More flexible matching with partial name prefix matching - Better chance of finding correct user without fallback ```
---
## Example Database Entries
### Database Setup ``` User ID | First Name | Last Name ---------|-------------|---------- 1 | Eva | Karimi 2 | John | Smith 3 | Stephen | Mungai 4 | David | Smith 5 | Karimi | Njagi ```
### Matching Results
#### Query 1: "Eva Karimi Njagi" ``` Attempt 1: Eva + Karimi → SELECT * FROM users WHERE first_name='eva' AND last_name='karimi' → FOUND: User ID 1 ✅ → Return: Eva Karimi ```
#### Query 2: "John Smith Johnson" ``` Attempt 1: John + Smith → SELECT * FROM users WHERE first_name='john' AND last_name='smith' → FOUND: User ID 2 ✅ → Return: John Smith ```
#### Query 3: "Karimi Njagi" ``` Attempt 1: Karimi + Njagi → SELECT * FROM users WHERE first_name='karimi' AND last_name='njagi' → NOT FOUND ❌
Attempt 2: (None - only 2 parts) → Use legacy fallback strategies → FOUND: User ID 5 ✅ (via partial matching) → Return: Karimi Njagi ```
#### Query 4: "David Karimi Smith" ``` Attempt 1: David + Karimi → SELECT * FROM users WHERE first_name='david' AND last_name='karimi' → NOT FOUND ❌
Attempt 2: David + Smith → SELECT * FROM users WHERE first_name='david' AND last_name='smith' → FOUND: User ID 4 ✅ → Return: David Smith ```
---
## Log Output Examples
### Before ``` [USER-MATCH] Matched 'John Smith' by parsed first+last: John Smith -> 1 [USER-FALLBACK] Using default user for 'Stephen Mungai' -> 999 ```
### After ``` [USER-MATCH] Matched 'John Smith' by parsed first+last: John Smith -> 1 [USER-MATCH] Matched 'Stephen Mungai' by parsed first+last (Stephen+Mungai): Stephen Mungai -> 3 [USER-MATCH] Matched 'Eva Karimi Njagi' by parsed first+last (Eva+Karimi): Eva Karimi -> 1 ```
### Verbose Mode ``` [USER-MATCH] Matched 'Eva Karimi Njagi' by parsed first+last (Eva+Karimi): Eva Karimi -> 1 - Strategy: multi-part-combinations - Tried: Eva+Karimi (1/3) ```
---
## Troubleshooting
### Issue: User still falling back to default ``` Name: "Stephen Mungai" Database: No entry for "Stephen" as first_name
Solution: 1. Check exact spelling in database (case-sensitive initially, then case-insensitive) 2. Verify first_name and last_name fields are populated 3. Check if name should be "Steve" instead of "Stephen" 4. Run verification script: rails runner scripts/verify_and_fix_user_assignments.rb ```
### Issue: Wrong user matched ``` Name: "John Smith" Database: Multiple users with "John" and "Smith"
The system will match the FIRST result from database query. To fix: 1. Use more specific names in JIRA 2. Update database with distinguishing middle names/initials 3. Use config map to manually specify: {Stephen Mungai: user_id_42} ```
---
## Statistics Report Example
``` USER MATCH STATISTICS REPORT ================================================================================ Total user lookups performed: 815
Match breakdown: ✅ Email matches: 16 (1.96%) ✅ Full name matches: 0 (0.0%) ✅ First+Last matches: 750 (92.02%) ✅ Partial matches: 0 (0.0%) ✅ Config map matches: 0 Created users: 0 ⚠️ Fallback to default: 49
Summary: Total unique matched users: 10 Total unique fallback uses: 1
Multi-part names parsed: standard-split: 8 name(s) dot-separated: 1 name(s) multi-part-combinations: 1 name(s) ← NEW! - 'Eva Karimi Njagi' → tries: [Eva+Karimi, Eva+Njagi, Karimi+Njagi]
Names that could not be matched (fell back to default user): - 'Stephen Mungai' (49 occurrences) ```
---
## Performance Notes
### Lookups per Name ``` Two-part name: ~3 DB queries (exact + 2 partial) Three-part name: ~9 DB queries (3 strategies × 3 queries each) Four-part name: ~12 DB queries (4 strategies × 3 queries each) ```
### Optimization: Short-Circuit on First Match ``` Once a match is found for ANY combination, the loop exits immediately. Most names match on the first strategy, so additional combinations are rarely tried. ```
### Caching (Future Enhancement) ``` Could cache successful matches to avoid repeated lookups: cache['Stephen Mungai'] = user_id_3
Estimated 70-80% cache hit rate for typical imports. ```
---
**Last Updated:** November 27, 2025 **Version:** 1.0

# Rich Text Table Handling in Jira Import ## Overview The `repair_rich_text_content.rb` script ensures that all content from Jira (including tables) is properly captured and stored in the database as rich HTML. ## How Tables Are Handled ### 1. **Jira Rendered HTML (Primary Method)** When available, the script uses Jira's pre-rendered HTML which includes fully formatted tables: ```ruby # For descriptions: jira_issue.dig('renderedFields', 'description') # For comments: jira_comment['renderedBody'] ``` **Advantages:** - ✅ Perfect fidelity - exactly as Jira renders it - ✅ Includes all formatting: tables, lists, code blocks, colors, etc. - ✅ No conversion needed ### 2. **ADF to HTML Conversion (Fallback)** If rendered HTML is not available, the script converts Jira's ADF (Atlassian Document Format) to HTML: ```ruby def convert_adf_table_to_html(table_block) # Handles: # - tableRow / tablerow # - tableHeader / tablehead / tableHead # - tableCell # Outputs:
......
end ``` **Table HTML Output:** ```html
Header 1 Header 2
Cell 1 Cell 2
``` ## Usage ### Basic Usage (Single Project) ```bash # Repair all content for KCBL project bin/rails runner scripts/repair_rich_text_content.rb KCBL ``` ### With Debug Mode ```bash # See detailed logging about HTML extraction DEBUG=true bin/rails runner scripts/repair_rich_text_content.rb KCBL ``` Debug mode shows: - `[Using rendered HTML]` - When Jira's pre-rendered HTML is used (preferred) - `[Using ADF conversion]` - When ADF needs to be converted - Comment-level details ### With Environment Variables ```bash # Using environment variables PROJECT=KCBL bin/rails runner scripts/repair_rich_text_content.rb # Or JIRA_PROJECT=KCBL DEBUG=true bin/rails runner scripts/repair_rich_text_content.rb ``` ### All Projects ```bash # Process all projects (no filter) bin/rails runner scripts/repair_rich_text_content.rb ``` ## Verification ### Check If Tables Were Captured ```ruby # In Rails console: defect = Defect.find_by(defect_unique: 'KCBL-123') puts defect.content # Should show tags if tables exist # Or check comments: defect.defect_messages.each do |msg| puts "Has table: #{msg.content.include?(' tags ``` 4. **Re-run the repair script:** The script compares normalized HTML, so if content differs, it will update: ```bash bin/rails runner scripts/repair_rich_text_content.rb YOUR-PROJECT ``` ### Common Issues #### Issue: "Tables not appearing in UI" **Cause:** View layer may need table styling **Solution:** Check that ActionText/Trix or your rich text renderer supports tables #### Issue: "ADF conversion used instead of rendered HTML" **Cause:** Jira API might not be returning `renderedFields` **Solution:** - Verify `expand: 'renderedFields'` is in API request - Check Jira API permissions - Use DEBUG mode to confirm #### Issue: "Content says 'OK' but tables still missing" **Cause:** Normalized comparison considers content equal **Solution:** - Check actual content in database - May need to force update by temporarily changing comparison logic ## API Details ### Jira API Endpoints Used **Issue with rendered description:** ``` GET /rest/api/3/issue/{issueKey}?expand=renderedFields&fields=*all ``` **Comments with rendered body:** ``` GET /rest/api/3/issue/{issueKey}/comment?expand=renderedBody ``` ### Response Structure **Rendered Description:** ```json { "renderedFields": { "description": "

Text with

...

" } } ``` **Rendered Comment:** ```json { "comments": [ { "id": "123", "renderedBody": "

Comment with ...

", "body": { /* ADF structure */ } } ] } ``` ## Summary ✅ **Tables ARE captured** when using rendered HTML (default/preferred) ✅ **Tables ARE converted** when using ADF fallback ✅ **Both methods preserve table structure** The script prioritizes Jira's rendered HTML to ensure perfect fidelity, including tables, lists, code blocks, colors, and all other formatting.

#!/usr/bin/env bash # Collects SMTP/network diagnostics for a given SMTP host # Usage: ./scripts/smtp_debug.sh smtp.example.com
set -eu
SMTP_HOST=${1:-smtp6.relay.iad3b.emailsrvr.com} LOGDIR=/tmp OUTFILE="$LOGDIR/smtp-debug-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).txt" TIMEOUT_CMD="timeout 8s"
echo "SMTP debug run for: $SMTP_HOST" | tee "$OUTFILE" echo "Started at: $(date -u) (UTC)" | tee -a "$OUTFILE" echo "Hostname: $(hostname -f)" | tee -a "$OUTFILE" echo "Local IPs:" | tee -a "$OUTFILE" ip -4 addr show | sed -n '1,200p' | tee -a "$OUTFILE"
echo -e "\n=== DNS resolution ===" | tee -a "$OUTFILE" echo "dig A:" | tee -a "$OUTFILE" dig +short "$SMTP_HOST" | tee -a "$OUTFILE"
echo "dig ANY (caution):" | tee -a "$OUTFILE" dig +nocmd "$SMTP_HOST" any +noall +answer | tee -a "$OUTFILE"
echo -e "\n=== MX for your sending domain (replace example.com if needed) ===" | tee -a "$OUTFILE" echo "Run: dig +short MX your.domain" | tee -a "$OUTFILE"
echo -e "\n=== TCP port probes (nc) ===" | tee -a "$OUTFILE" for PORT in 25 587 465; do echo -e "\n-- nc -vz $SMTP_HOST $PORT --" | tee -a "$OUTFILE" $TIMEOUT_CMD nc -vz "$SMTP_HOST" $PORT 2>&1 | tee -a "$OUTFILE" || true done
echo -e "\n=== OpenSSL STARTTLS (587) ===" | tee -a "$OUTFILE" $TIMEOUT_CMD openssl s_client -starttls smtp -crlf -connect "$SMTP_HOST":587 </dev/null 2>&1 | sed -n '1,120p' | tee -a "$OUTFILE" || true
echo -e "\n=== OpenSSL SMTPS (465) ===" | tee -a "$OUTFILE" $TIMEOUT_CMD openssl s_client -connect "$SMTP_HOST":465 -crlf </dev/null 2>&1 | sed -n '1,120p' | tee -a "$OUTFILE" || true
echo -e "\n=== telnet probe (25) ===" | tee -a "$OUTFILE" $TIMEOUT_CMD bash -c "(echo EHLO $(hostname -s); sleep 1) | telnet $SMTP_HOST 25" 2>&1 | sed -n '1,120p' | tee -a "$OUTFILE" || true
echo -e "\n=== traceroute to host (TCP port 25) ===" | tee -a "$OUTFILE" if command -v traceroute >/dev/null 2>&1; then # Use TCP traceroute if available traceroute -T -p 25 "$SMTP_HOST" 2>&1 | tee -a "$OUTFILE" || true else echo "traceroute not found" | tee -a "$OUTFILE" fi
echo -e "\n=== Router/gateway / iptables / ufw ===" | tee -a "$OUTFILE" if command -v sudo >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "sudo iptables -L -n --line-numbers" | tee -a "$OUTFILE" sudo iptables -L -n --line-numbers 2>&1 | tee -a "$OUTFILE" || true echo -e "\nCheck nftables:" | tee -a "$OUTFILE" sudo nft list ruleset 2>&1 | sed -n '1,120p' | tee -a "$OUTFILE" || true echo -e "\nUFW status:" | tee -a "$OUTFILE" sudo ufw status verbose 2>&1 | tee -a "$OUTFILE" || true else echo "sudo not available for firewall checks; run iptables/nft/ufw manually as root" | tee -a "$OUTFILE" fi
echo -e "\n=== Local listeners (ss) ===" | tee -a "$OUTFILE" ss -ltnp 2>&1 | egrep ":25 |:465 |:587 " || ss -ltnp 2>&1 | tee -a "$OUTFILE" || true
echo -e "\n=== Check cloud provider outbound filter (simple external probe) ===" | tee -a "$OUTFILE" echo "Trying to connect to smtp.gmail.com:25 and :587" | tee -a "$OUTFILE" for HOST in smtp.gmail.com; do for PORT in 25 587; do echo "nc -vz $HOST $PORT" | tee -a "$OUTFILE" $TIMEOUT_CMD nc -vz $HOST $PORT 2>&1 | tee -a "$OUTFILE" || true done done
echo -e "\n=== Summary lines to search for ===" | tee -a "$OUTFILE" echo "Search the logfile for: '554', 'Connection refused', 'failed to open TCP connection', 'Net::SMTP'" | tee -a "$OUTFILE"
echo -e "\nOutput saved to: $OUTFILE" | tee -a "$OUTFILE"
# Print the path for convenience echo "$OUTFILE"
exit 0
